clue.text: No problem for the vicar, then, in 3 12's 21

definitions.text: No problem for the vicar, then
definitions.meaning: a vicar's benefice is called his living, so a vicar without trouble has an easy one
the opening line of the song Summertime from the Gershwin opera runs 'Summertime, and ...' with these words

explanation.walkthrough: The cross-references point to PORGY AND BESS (3, 12) and SUMMER (21): the lyric comes from the song Summertime. A clergyman's paid post is traditionally his 'living'.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a lyric from the song Summertime and, read literally, describes a comfortable clerical benefice.

clue.text: Musician to suit change in residence

indicators.note: in places the rearranged letters within the word for a residence

parts.note: a flat is a place of residence

indicators.note: change tells us to rearrange the letters of suit

explanation.surface: A performer is told to alter their outfit while staying at home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is only a link; 'residence' as a home makes it look like the flute player is moving house.
explanation.definitionFit: A flute player is a kind of musician.

clue.text: 17 down's monarchs in 1952?

parts.note: the composer's opera title read as pet names of King George VI (Georgie Porgie) and Elizabeth (Bess), who succeeded him in 1952

explanation.surface: A question about which kings and queens a composer had in a particular year.
explanation.walkthrough: 17 down is GERSHWIN. In 1952 George VI died and Elizabeth II came to the throne; the nursery-rhyme 'Georgie Porgie' and the pet name Bess fit the two monarchs.
explanation.definitionFit: The title of the Gershwin opera can be read as nicknames for a George and an Elizabeth, the two British monarchs of that year.

clue.text: Consent to investigation? I don't know

definitions.meaning: an invitation to be frisked: go ahead, look through my pockets
a casual way of saying you have no idea

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase literally invites a frisk and idiomatically means you have no answer to offer.

clue.text: Not just brunette?

definitions.meaning: fair can mean light-haired, so a dark-haired person is jokingly the opposite of fair

explanation.definitionFit: Unjust is a plain synonym, while 'fair' meaning blond gives the playful second reading for a dark-haired person.

clue.text: V1 causing double trouble in a friend

indicators.note: in places the stirred-up letters within the animal

parts.note: the dog is man's best friend

indicators.note: trouble means the letters of double are stirred up

explanation.surface: A German weapon is blamed for causing a pal twice the usual difficulties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'causing' is a link; 'a friend' is the dog, man's best friend, and 'trouble' is the anagram signal rather than a noun of the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: The V1 flying bomb of the Second World War was nicknamed the doodlebug by Londoners.

clue.text: Setter's funny way

indicators.note: funny suggests the letters of the word setter are put into an odd new order

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: The crossword compiler has a peculiar manner.
explanation.walkthrough: The possessive 's adds no letter: 'funny' rearranges SETTER.
explanation.definitionFit: A street is a road, and way is a common word for a road in names.

clue.text: Let person open it? Maybe better not

definitions.text: Let person open it? Maybe better not

indicators.note: maybe suggests the preceding words could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Advice about whether to let someone open a suspicious envelope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Maybe' rearranges the fifteen letters of LET PERSON OPEN IT; the whole clue also describes the nasty anonymous letter you would rather not open.
explanation.definitionFit: An anonymous malicious letter is exactly the kind of mail it would be better for the recipient not to open.

clue.text: Everyone's in debt when there's a female around — when there's witches around!

indicators.note: around says the female bird goes about the phrase meaning everyone is in debt

parts.note: a hen is a female bird
everyone gives all; the 's is read as is
to be in debt is to owe

explanation.surface: A grim financial picture, then a spooky echo of it with witches instead of females.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's in 'Everyone's' stands for 'is', so the phrase reads as a little sentence: everybody owes.
explanation.definitionFit: The night of 31 October is traditionally when witches and ghosts are abroad.

clue.text: Excel, alfresco or not

indicators.note: not tells us to take away the letters of the word or

parts.note: alfresco means in the open air, outdoor
taken as written

explanation.surface: Being brilliant whether in the open air or indoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' removes OR from the end of OUTDOOR.
explanation.definitionFit: To surpass someone is to do better than them, which is what excelling means.

clue.text: Turn in — more time in suitable chair

indicators.note: in places the turn within the word for more time

parts.note: longer means for more time
a turn is a U, as in U-turn

explanation.surface: Someone going to bed late in a comfortable seat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turn' gives U, as in a U-turn, and 'in' puts it inside LONGER; the second 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A lounger is a reclining chair, apt for stretching out on.

clue.text: See 3
Obsolete coin with nothing in it? Precisely

annotationWithheld.why: Obsolete coin with nothing in it? Precisely (4) for VOID: 'Obsolete' and 'with nothing in it' both mean void, but no parse found gives 'coin' a job
annotationWithheld.clue: Obsolete coin with nothing in it? Precisely

clue.text: Dance scene in 3 12 in case ferryman comes round

indicators.note: comes round says the ferryman surrounds the phrase for in case

parts.note: Charon is the ferryman of the dead in Greek myth
lest means in case

explanation.surface: A setting in an opera where a boatman arrives just in case.
explanation.walkthrough: 3 12 is PORGY AND BESS, which is set in Catfish Row in this South Carolina city, also the name of a 1920s dance.
explanation.definitionFit: It is both a lively 1920s dance and the city where the Gershwin opera is set.

clue.text: Flickers of anger during escape

indicators.note: during places anger inside the escape

parts.note: flight is an escape
ire is anger

explanation.surface: Bursts of temper flare up while running away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' is a link; the definition is a plural verb read loosely, as the light of a fire flickers.
explanation.definitionFit: The light from a fire is unsteady and dancing, so it is a flickering glow.

clue.text: Compound report of journey in the dark

indicators.note: report of means we hear the phrase spoken

parts.note: a night ride is a journey after dark

explanation.surface: An account of travelling at night.
explanation.definitionFit: A nitride is a chemical compound of nitrogen with another element.

clue.text: Method of painting sticky stuff sounds a pain

indicators.note: sounds tells us the word for sticky stuff is spoken, not spelt

parts.note: goo is sticky stuff
an ache is a pain

explanation.surface: A painting technique involving gunk turns out to be agony.
explanation.definitionFit: Gouache is a technique using opaque watercolour paints.

clue.text: Musician to spread her wings?

indicators.note: to spread suggests the letters of her wings are opened out into a new order

explanation.surface: A performer encouraged to take flight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to spread' rearranges HER WINGS into the composer's name.
explanation.definitionFit: George Gershwin was an American composer and pianist.

clue.text: See 26
I'm calling with a certain qualification

parts.note: I am calling read as I name
sure means certain

explanation.surface: Someone phoning and attaching a caveat.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'I'm calling' as 'I name', so I + NAME, then A and SURE.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means to some extent, the kind of hedge that limits how far a statement holds.

clue.text: An aura not born of hostility

parts.note: an gives the article a

indicators.note: not says the abbreviation for born is dropped

parts.note: a nimbus is a halo or aura

explanation.surface: Ill feeling that did not originate from a glowing halo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' removes B from NIMBUS, leaving NIMUS; 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Animus is a feeling of strong dislike or ill will.

clue.text: "___ born great", said Malvolio, the mathematician

indicators.note: said Malvolio means the quoted words are spoken aloud

parts.note: the missing words in Malvolio's line 'some are born great' are some are

explanation.surface: A quotation from Twelfth Night with a gap to fill.
explanation.walkthrough: In Twelfth Night Malvolio reads 'some are born great'; spoken, 'some are' runs together into the word for one who adds up.
explanation.definitionFit: A summer is jokingly one who does sums, a person working at arithmetic.

clue.text: A lake fed by a river (more like the Dead Sea?)

indicators.note: fed by says the lake takes in the river between its letters

explanation.surface: A lake supplied by a river is compared with a salty sea.
explanation.walkthrough: The Aral Sea, in Central Asia, has shrunk and become far saltier, so it is now more like the Dead Sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The Aral Sea has shrivelled and grown very salty, making it resemble the lifeless salt lake of the Middle East.

clue.text: Joins scandal up?

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the word is read upwards

parts.note: a stink is a scandal or fuss

explanation.surface: Asks whether someone links up with a scandal.
explanation.definitionFit: To knit is to join or bond together, as broken bones knit.

clue.text: Take your place in the distance with return to streaming?

indicators.note: with return tells us the whole assembly is read backwards
in puts the word for taking a seat inside the distance

parts.note: a mile is a distance
to take your place is to sit

explanation.surface: Being seated far away and then coming back to the stream.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link. 'streaming' means sorting school pupils by ability, not flowing water, and the question mark flags the loose definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Streaming in schools groups pupils by ability, which critics call favouring a select few.

clue.text: Leader of Leeds in the Sun — wrong part of Leeds

indicators.note: in puts that first letter inside the rearranged words
wrong suggests the letters of the Sun are jumbled
leader of picks the first letter of Leeds

explanation.surface: A Leeds figure basking in the sun, then a wrong turn in Leeds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' turns THE SUN into HUNSET, and 'in' places L, the leader of Leeds, inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Hunslet is a district of the city of Leeds in Yorkshire.

clue.text: Co-author slain horribly around 14

indicators.note: horribly suggests the letters of co-author and slain are mangled

explanation.surface: A writing partner meets a nasty end near a dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 14 is CHARLESTON, a city in this US state; 'horribly' rearranges CO-AUTHOR SLAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Charleston is a city in this US state, so the state is the area around it.

clue.text: Being old, have gun when diamonds are about

parts.note: ex means former or old

indicators.note: are about says the diamonds surround the gun

parts.note: ice is slang for diamonds
a Sten is a British submachine gun

explanation.surface: An elderly person armed with a gun while gems are nearby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'have' and 'when' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Existence is the state of being alive or real.
